 Updated 2027 NFL Draft Order After Week 10 Results, Who Could Dolphins & Titans Take?
 Joe Tansey Nov 15, 2026 
 The Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins kept themselves in contention for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft with losses in Sunday's early afternoon window.
 The Titans and Dolphins are both now 1-8 and a half-game behind the Los Angeles Chargers in the standings. The Chargers play the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night. 
 The New York Jets' own first-round pick is now up to No. 4 in the projected order. The Jets have three total picks in the top 13 right now because they own the Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys' first-round selections.
 The Titans, Dolphins and Jets will be at the forefront of the quarterback market, but it's still to be determined which college signal-caller tops draft boards.

 Drew Mestemaker
 2 of 3 AP Photo 
 Drew Mestemaker leads the FBS in passing yards and passing touchdowns. 
 The Oklahoma State quarterback surged up draft boards in the last month due to his performances and the lack of success from other signal-callers in the draft class. 
 Mestemaker didn't have the best game on Saturday against the Texas Tech Red Raiders. He threw for 277 yards, but he was picked off twice and completed just 64.3 percent of his passes. 
 Saturday marked just the second time all season in which Mestemaker failed to throw for 300 yards. He's only been under 250 passing yards once. 
 The consistency throughout the year in a pass-friendly offense has made Mestemaker an intriguing prospect to NFL personnel.
 Miami, Tennessee and the New York Jets could all be in the market for Mestemaker because of their current quarterback situations. 
 The Los Angeles Chargers likely won't go after the Oklahoma State quarterback because of the money attached to Justin Herbert. 
 Leonard Moore
 3 of 3 AP Photo 
 Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore is one of the best defensive options in the draft class. 
 Moore has 19 tackles, five passes defended and a forced fumble for the fifth-ranked Fighting Irish.
 Moore and Texas Longhorns edge rusher Colin Simmons are two of the best defensive prospects that serve as an alternative to Jeremiah Smith or any available quarterback. 
 Moore might be a better option for the New York Jets because they have multiple first-round draft picks.
 However, if the Titans want to hold on to Cam Ward, they would be smart to invest their defense and Moore would be under strong consideration.
